title: Copernicus: NASA's Deep-Space Trajectory Designer
description: Copernicus is NASA Johnson's trajectory design and optimization system for complex deep-space missions: it chains segments — launches, flybys, burns — into a mission and optimizes the whole thing. Multi-body, multi-revolution, low-thrust problems are its home. It is the tool behind serious interplanetary design work at JSC.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Segments: The Unit of Design
description: A Copernicus segment is one piece of trajectory — a coast arc, a burn, a flyby — with its own propagator, controls, and constraints. Segments link at boundaries where position, velocity, and time must match. Designing a mission is designing segments and their handshakes.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Multiple Shooting Optimization
description: Copernicus optimizes with multiple shooting: the trajectory is broken into segments, each propagated independently, and the optimizer drives the boundary mismatches to zero while minimizing fuel or time. Parallel segments converge faster than one long propagation. It is the workhorse algorithm of modern trajectory design.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Gravity Assists and Flybys
description: A gravity assist steals momentum from a planet: arrive on the right hyperbola, leave faster in the right direction, spending no propellant. Copernicus targets flyby aim points (B-plane) to chain assists across the solar system. Voyager's grand tour is the legendary example; every outer-planet mission uses the trick.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Low-Thrust Trajectories
description: Electric propulsion thrusts for months, spiraling outward — Copernicus optimizes low-thrust arcs where impulsive approximations fail. The control is a continuous thrust direction history, not a few burns. Dawn's ion-propelled tour of Vesta and Ceres proved the regime.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Multi-Body Dynamics
description: Beyond Earth, one-body math fails: Copernicus propagates in multi-body gravity — Sun, planets, moons together — where Lagrange points and weak-stability boundaries live. Halo orbits around Sun-Earth L1/L2 (SOHO, JWST) are multi-body designs. The patched-conic sketch gets you close; multi-body gets you there.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Mission Phases and Constraints
description: Copernicus missions carry real constraints: launch windows, arrival dates, lighting at arrival, comms geometry, propellant caps. Constraints are first-class — the optimizer respects them or reports infeasibility. Designing to constraints is what separates studies from missions.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Plotting and Visualization
description: Copernicus visualizes trajectories in 3D — porkchop plots of launch/arrival energy, B-plane targets, ground tracks — because designers think in pictures before numbers. A porkchop plot picks the launch window at a glance. Visualization is analysis, not decoration.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Launch Windows and C3
description: C3 (launch energy) measures how hard a mission leaves Earth — higher C3 needs a bigger rocket or a smaller spacecraft. Copernicus searches launch dates for minimum C3 to the target. Windows repeat with planetary synodic periods; missing one can mean waiting years.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Arrival: Insertion and Capture
description: Arriving is a maneuver: orbit insertion burns brake the spacecraft into capture, sized by the arrival hyperbola. Copernicus targets insertion conditions — periapsis altitude, inclination — and the capture burn that achieves them. Too fast an arrival means too big a brake.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Station-Keeping in Deep Space
description: Halo and libration orbits need station-keeping — small maneuvers fighting instability, targeted with Copernicus-class tools. JWST's halo around Sun-Earth L2 gets periodic trims. Unstable orbits are useful precisely because they are cheap to reach and shape.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Trade Studies: The Design Space
description: Copernicus runs trade studies — chemical vs electric, direct vs flyby, fast vs efficient — mapping the design space before committing. Trades are quantified: years vs tons vs dollars. The tool's speed makes broad exploration possible; judgment picks the point.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Verification of Trajectory Designs
description: Trajectory designs verify by independent propagation: rebuild the mission in a second tool and compare. Boundary mismatches, constraint violations, and fuel accounting get checked to the meter and the kilogram. Two tools agreeing is the standard.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Copernicus in Mission Proposals
description: Discovery and New Frontiers proposals live or die on trajectory credibility — Copernicus-class analysis proves the mission fits the rocket, the timeline, and the fuel budget. Reviewers trust optimized, constrained designs. The tool turns ideas into fundable missions.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Copernicus Design Loop
description: Ladder-top Copernicus: sketch segments, link boundaries, shoot and optimize, check constraints, study trades, verify independently, and fly the design. Fifteen rungs from porkchop plots to interplanetary missions.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
